summary: Lewis County, WA summit site: L-4 cab dated 1930, Aircraft Warning Service post 1942-44, cab removed or destroyed in the 1960s; reached by trail, no lookout standing.

facts.status_note: Cab removed or destroyed in the 1960s; no source describes a standing structure, only a photo captioned as a lookout front step

staffing.status: Aircraft Warning Service spotting post 1942-44; closure announced for summer 1964 except possible emergency use; no later fire staffing described

access.note: On Monument land reached by trail; the easiest approach starts on Weyerhaeuser land and needs a Longview-St Helens access permit or key (Willhite)

visit.trail_note: Day hike from the Goat Mountain trail per WTA; Willhite gives 2 miles from the permit area and 6.5 miles from the Goat Creek trailhead

events.note: L-4 cab. Register and firelookout.com give 1930; Willhite says likely 1930
Photos taken when the site was a camp, before the cab (Willhite)
Aircraft Warning Service spotting post; Seattle Filter Center activated it March 19, 1942
Aircraft Warning Service post deactivated April 1, 1944
May 1964 newspaper item (dated May 5, 1964) says it will be closed that summer except for possible emergency use; the sources do not confirm the closure happened
Year is a placeholder for the decade: sources say only sometime in the 1960s. Register says removed rather than destroyed
Registered July 18, 2012 as FFLOS US 1350, WA 250

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register says the cab was removed in the 1960s; firelookout.com and Willhite say it was destroyed sometime in that decade. The story reports both and gives no exact year.
The register and firelookout.com give 1930 flatly; Willhite says likely 1930. The story keeps the 1930 date with the hedge.

sources.title: Vanson Peak Lookout Site - Vanson Lake

notes_for_editor: Brief access 'unknown' is now public (Monument trail) with the Weyerhaeuser permit caveat from Willhite. The 1960 event year is a placeholder for an undated 1960s removal; treat it as decade-only. The 1942-44 post was an Aircraft Warning Service spotting post, not a fire lookout, and no fires are described at this site in the sources read. The 1964 item is a May announcement; no source confirms closure. Read 6 pages and ran 1 websearch.
